subject: Post-call: ACME inference evaluation — interoperability playbook & next tests
messages:
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Sofia Kendall <sofia.kendall@acme.com>; Ryan Chen <ryan.chen@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 21 Aug 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: ACME inference evaluation — interoperability playbook & next tests

Thanks again for the call this morning — great alignment on scope and success criteria. Quick recap and a pragmatic set of next tests so we can validate parity against your hyperscaler baseline and the other inference APIs you mentioned.

Summary of what we heard:
- Primary goals: streaming latency under 150ms tail for 99th pct, reliable function/tool calling with schema fidelity, and predictable token cost per session.
- Current comparison targets: AWS Bedrock (realtime pipeline), OpenAI endpoints, and your internal on-prem inference for PII-sensitive flows.
- Constraints: data residency in us-east-1 for pilot, SOC2 evidence required, and procurement timeline roughly 6–8 weeks.

Redwood differentiators we discussed (short):
- Deterministic routing + fallback to quantized variants to keep apps online when capacity shifts.
- Built-in structured output validation for function/tool calling (schema enforcement + explainability hooks).
- Streaming with prefix/KV caching to reduce cost while meeting latency SLOs.
- Per-token cost breakdown and autoscaling policies tailored to interactive workloads.

Proposed next tests (attached matrix):
A) Streaming parity: run 2k concurrent short-turn streams (avg 12 tokens/turn) vs your Bedrock baseline. Measure p50/p95/p99 tail latencies and token egress.
B) Tool/function-calling fidelity: execute 150 schema-driven calls (external tool stubs) and check JSON schema conformance and hallucination rate on tool args.
C) Structured-output stress: evaluate large JSON payloads (nested lists) and extraction correctness under both standard FP and int8-quantized paths.

Asks from ACME for next week:
- A short test dataset (sample prompts + expected schema for tool calls).
- Temporary evaluation keys or a neutral proxy endpoint we can hit.
- Any compliance docs we should review (we'll provide SOC2 artifact pointers after NDA).

I attached an initial interop-test-matrix and sketched mutual-action-plan. Monica and Marcus will own the test execution and instrumentation; Grace will own compliance coordination.

Proposed timeline:
- Kickoff test call: Tue Aug 24, 2026 — 60 min (we can schedule 9–11am PT)
- Tests run: Aug 25–27
- Debrief: Aug 28 (15–30 min) with preliminary metrics

Sofia/Ryan — does this plan align with your priorities? If yes, I'll lock the kickoff slot and Monica will share specific test payloads.

Thanks,

Dylan Brooks
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
Mobile: (415) 555-0198

Subject: Re: Post-call: ACME inference evaluation — interoperability playbook & next tests

Thanks, Dylan — this looks good. A few quick clarifications from our side before the kickoff:

1) Streaming latency: our internal SLA target is p99 < 120ms for our interactive UI. We understand the costs of KV caching but want the baseline numbers without caching and then with Redwood's recommended cache configs.
2) Function calling: we have three critical tool schemas (order_create, user_lookup, pricing_estimate). We'll share a zipped set of sample payloads and expected schema files by EOD today.
3) Data residency: must be hosted in us-east-1 for the pilot (we cannot route telemetry outside the region). Does Redwood support a per-tenant regional pinning for pilot accounts?

Also: we've started an internal procurement checklist — I'll attach the top-level doc in a separate email. Looking forward to the kickoff.

Sofia Kendall

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Date: Mon, 24 Aug 2026 09:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: ACME inference evaluation — interoperability playbook & next tests

Great — thanks for the rapid reply, Sofia. Per your asks, a few concrete notes and the test spec we'll use (high-level):

Streaming parity (Test A):
- Two runs:
  1) No-prefix-cache run: single-stream latency measurement at 100/500/2k concurrent sessions. Measure p50/p95/p99 token-to-token latency and end-to-end response time.
  2) Cache-enabled run: enable prefix/KV cache consistent with Redwood's prod config and repeat.
- Inputs: short prompts (10–25 tokens seed). We'll provision a test harness and provide a script to replay traces so you can run identical traces against Bedrock and OpenAI.

Function/tool-calling (Test B):
- Implement our function-calling shim that logs: (a) raw LLM output, (b) parsed JSON, (c) validation errors against the provided JSON schema.
- Acceptance criteria: >= 98% schema conformance across 150 calls; less than 2% critical hallucinations (erroneous tool args).

Structured-output stress (Test C):
- 60 payloads with nested arrays and optional fields; validate extraction accuracy and size-related truncation behavior across quantized vs FP paths.

Operational asks from ACME for test setup:
- Temporary eval API key or IP allowlist for our harness (we will not store keys beyond test window).
- A small set of reference transcripts with expected parse results (zip).
- Confirmation that region pinning to us-east-1 is acceptable for the pilot; we support per-tenant regional pin via our VPC/private deployment layer for pilots — Grace will follow up with an architecture note and SOC2 artifact pointers.

I've attached the detailed interop-test-matrix (workbook) and a one-page test checklist. Marcus will run the streaming harness; I'll run the function-calling evaluation and coordinate metrics ingestion into the Redwood Console.

Proposed kickoff: Tue Aug 24, 09:30am PT — does that work for ACME?

Thanks,

Monica Patel
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
